plan:
# Pipeline panel session, 2026-10-31

## Pitch

**Color grading specialist:** Two-tone run sheet. I'd build it twice. Version A puts the step list first and the log second. Version B makes the log the hero and shrinks the steps to a strip. Same failed Test step, same glyphs, two hierarchies on one grey scale. Components: step list, log pane, retry button, pass check, duration strip, theme pair. It has to look good at 2 a.m. with a failed build on screen. Small option one: a 2px rule on the failed row. Small option two: a slightly darker surface behind it. I'd back the rule.

**Wayfinding designer:** Signal edge. One quiet surface for the whole panel. The failed step owns a single strong edge, the left 2px bar, and nothing else is loud. A stranger opens the panel. What do they expect next? The cause, then a button. So the order is step, log, retry, result. Components: step rail, log tail, retry, result line, attempt history, a legend for the glyph shapes. It should still read in five years. No ornament that dates.

**Camera operator:** Single frame. Everything that matters fits in one 360px column at first paint. Failure already expanded, log already scrolled to the error line. Then I break the frame once: the retry output streams into the log, and the check draws out of the row's glyph slot. That's the only motion. Hidden cost: auto-scroll fights anyone reading up. Components: step rail, log tail with jump-to-error, morphing retry, pass check, compact header, keyboard hint strip.

**Amber crab:** Side doors. The one who finds this panel wants out of the failure. Forward is Retry. Sideways is "retry from here", "retry everything" and "look at the last attempt". Side steps need the same weight as the step forward. Which action matters most? Retry this step. Everything else sits next to it, never under a menu. Components: retry scope choice, retry button, attempt history, step rail, log, result.

## Clash

**Camera operator:** Two versions costs us twice the states for one panel. Pick the hierarchy now. Step rail first, log under it. The failed row already gives the log its frame.

**Color grading specialist:** Fine. I ran both in my head and B buries which step failed. A wins. But the glyphs carry the state, never hue alone, and the accent stays one restrained blue.

**Wayfinding designer:** Agreed on one accent. The legend can go. If the shapes need a legend, the shapes are wrong. Each glyph gets its word next to it.

**Amber crab:** Then my scope choice. Is it a menu? A menu hides the side step. Three radio segments: This step, From here, Whole run.

**Camera operator:** Hidden cost: three segments beside Retry crowd 360px. Put them on their own line above the button, default This step. One line, no wrap.

**Wayfinding designer:** And attempt history earns a row only if it answers "did the retry fix it or did it just pass by luck". Same test failing twice is the thing a stranger can't see otherwise.

**Color grading specialist:** Then the result line says it outright: "Failed again · same test" or "Passed on attempt 2". The check draws once, 200ms. No glow.

**Amber crab:** Which action matters most when it fails again? Retry, still. Focus returns to it. History is the side door, one tab away.

## Decision

The team builds a pipeline status panel for a local build demo where a developer sees the failed Test step expanded on first paint, reads its log at the error line, chooses a retry scope, retries, and learns whether the fix held across attempts.

Concept: Signal Edge Run Panel

Wayfinding designer set the spine: one quiet surface, one 2px accent edge for selection, and the step, log, retry, result order. Color grading specialist tested two hierarchies and chose rail-over-log. She also fixed the single accent and the glyph-plus-word rule. Camera operator held the first frame to 360px with the failure pre-expanded. He limited motion to two moments, streamed log lines and one check stroke, and flagged the auto-scroll cost. That cost became a pause-on-scroll rule. Amber crab made retry scope a visible three-way choice and kept attempt history one Tab stop from Retry.

Rejected direction: the Camera operator's keyboard hint strip. Each component carries its own keyboard behaviour and focus ring. A permanent strip would cost 32px of the first frame for text most visitors read once.

No component_source was supplied. The inspiration paths for the CI oscilloscope, splitflap label button and rolling log band served as idea bank entries only. No code was taken. The three seeds from the 2026-10-30 popular snapshot are extended with new jobs. Morphing Action FAB becomes a retry-to-stop morph tied to a job. Success Check becomes an attempt verdict that also reports a repeated failure. Typewriter Loop becomes a log tail that streams real lines once and stops.

Six components earn their place, one per question. Where did it fail (rail). Why (log). How far to rerun (scope). Rerun (retry). Did it hold (result). Was it luck (history). Removing any one leaves a question unanswered. A seventh, the legend, was cut in the Clash.

## Build notes

1. First frame at 360px wide: rail with Test expanded (about 280px), scope line (40px), Retry (44px) and the log opened at line 212. The verdict line must sit above the fold. Test this with the log's minimum height set to 160px.
2. Log Follow logic: compare `scrollHeight - scrollTop - clientHeight` with 24px on every scroll event. Never call `scrollIntoView` while paused. Count appended lines into the 'Paused · n new lines' label.
3. One job object owns the AbortController, attempt id and scope list. Rows 3, 4 and 5 subscribe to it. Only the per-character draw of the newest log line and the single check stroke animate. Both are skipped under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.

expanded: a selected step open with its summary line, reached by click or Enter
collapsed: no step open, reached by toggling the open step
blocked: Package and Deploy preview show hollow-dash glyph and 'blocked by Test'
running: arc glyph on the retried step, reached when row 3 starts a run
focus: 2px accent ring at 2px offset, reached by Tab or arrows
reduced-motion: arc glyph static with the word 'running'

components.name: Log tail
components.description: Monospace log for the selected step that opens at the first error line and streams new lines once during a run.
components.purpose: Show why the step failed and what the retry is printing.
components.use: A developer reads line 212 'checkout.spec.ts › pays with saved card · timeout 5000 ms' highlighted on open.
components.input: Scroll with wheel or touch. Click or tap Jump to error or Follow. Keyboard: Tab focuses the log region, arrows and Page Up/Down scroll, E jumps to the next error line, F toggles Follow.
components.outcome: On open the view centres the first error line. During a run, new lines append at their sample arrival times and the view follows the tail.
components.recovery: Scrolling up during a run pauses Follow and shows 'Paused · 14 new lines' with a Follow button. Pressing it returns to the tail.
components.mechanism: A pre element in a focusable region with role log and tabindex 0. Line numbers come from a CSS counter, and long lines scroll horizontally without wrapping. Only the newest line draws its characters at 8 ms each, once. Earlier lines arrive whole and the caret disappears when the run ends. Follow is on while the scroll offset is within 24px of the bottom.
components.nearestAnalogue: 2026-10-30 link retype line typed one changed URL suffix. 2026-10-26 log viewer filtered past events. This row streams a live run once, pauses for a reader and finds error lines.
components.usefulness: The cause sits in the log. Opening at the error line saves scrolling past 200 lines of install output.
components.creativeDifference: Extends Typewriter Loop: typing appears only on the line being written now, so motion marks live output and stops with the run.
states: opened-at-error: line 212 highlighted and centred, reached on load
streaming: newest line types once with caret, reached by a row 3 run
paused: 'Paused · n new lines' with Follow, reached by scrolling up during a run
settled: caret removed, reached when the run ends
empty: 'Select a step', reached when no step is expanded
focus: 2px ring on the region
reduced-motion: new lines appear whole

components.name: Retry stop morph
components.description: Retry button whose glyph and label morph into Stop while the run is active and back when it ends.
components.purpose: Start one rerun of the chosen scope and offer a way to stop it from the same spot.
components.use: A developer presses Retry step, watches the log, then presses Stop when the same timeout appears early.
components.input: Click or tap the 44px button. Keyboard: Tab to it, Enter or Space. R retries when the panel has focus. Escape stops a running job.
components.outcome: Retry starts attempt n+1 with the scope from row 4. The circular-arrow glyph rotates into a square and the label changes from 'Retry step' to 'Stop' in a reserved width.
components.recovery: Stop aborts the run, marks the attempt 'stopped' and morphs back to Retry. A press during the 180 ms morph sets the final state directly. Focus returns to the button when a run ends.
components.mechanism: One native button bound to a job object with an AbortController and attempt id. Replies tagged with an older attempt id are dropped. The label width is reserved from its longest string, 'Retry from here'. The glyph strokes move in one transform transition.
components.nearestAnalogue: 2026-10-30 share morph trigger toggled a dialog open and closed. 2026-10-30 retry guard deduped a content request. This button morphs on job state and owns both start and abort.
components.usefulness: Keeping Stop in the same place as Retry means the developer never hunts for a cancel control mid-run.
components.creativeDifference: Extends Morphing Action FAB: the morph tracks whether a job is running, so the shape always tells the developer what a press will do.
states: ready: 'Retry step', reached on load and after any run ends
pressed: 1px sink, reached on pointer or key down
running: square glyph with 'Stop', reached on press
stopping: disabled 'Stopping', reached by Stop or Escape
scope-label: label reads 'Retry step', 'Retry from here' or 'Retry run' per row 4
focus: 2px ring
reduced-motion: glyph swaps without rotation

components.name: Retry scope
components.description: Three-way segmented choice for rerunning this step, this step and those after it, or the whole run.
components.purpose: Choose how much of the pipeline a retry reruns.
components.use: A developer suspects a stale build cache and picks 'Whole run' instead of 'This step'.
components.input: Click or tap a segment. Keyboard: Tab into the group, Left and Right move and select, Home and End jump.
components.outcome: The choice sets the rerun list. A note shows its cost from sample durations: 'Reruns Test · about 41 s', 'Reruns Test, Package, Deploy preview · about 70 s' or 'Reruns all 6 · about 2 min 3 s'.
components.recovery: The group is locked during a run, with a note 'Scope locked while running'. The last choice persists for the next retry.
components.mechanism: Native radio inputs styled as segments on one line with fixed label widths. Estimates are sums of the last recorded durations, labelled 'about'. When no step has failed, 'This step' and 'From here' are disabled.
components.nearestAnalogue: 2026-10-28 range selector is also a segmented radio group. That control changed a data window. This one sets the extent of a destructive rerun and shows its time cost.
components.usefulness: Rerunning only the failed step is fast but can hide cache problems. Seeing the cost helps the developer choose.
components.creativeDifference: Side steps get the same weight as the forward retry: all three options sit visible at one tap, none behind a menu.
states: default: 'This step' checked, reached on load
changed: new segment checked with updated estimate, reached by click or arrows
locked: disabled during a run
no-failure: only 'Whole run' enabled, reached after a full pass
focus: 2px ring on the checked segment

components.name: Attempt verdict
components.description: Result line that draws a check only on a confirmed pass and states whether a repeat failure matches the previous one.
components.purpose: Say how the latest attempt ended and whether the failure changed.
components.use: A developer reads 'Failed again · same test · checkout.spec.ts' and stops retrying.
components.input: Display only. Click or tap the failing test name to jump the row 2 log to it. Keyboard: Tab to the test name link, Enter.
components.outcome: On exit 0 the check stroke draws in 200 ms and the line reads 'Passed on attempt 2 · 39 s'. On failure it compares the failing test names with the previous attempt and reports 'same test', 'different error' or 'stopped'.
components.recovery: Stopped attempts read 'Stopped at 12 s · no verdict' and do not draw. A later pass replaces the line.
components.mechanism: Rendered from the final attempt record. Failing test names are compared as sets against the previous attempt. The line sits in a polite live region and announces once per attempt. The check is an SVG path with stroke-dashoffset animated once.
components.nearestAnalogue: 2026-10-30 copy check button drew a check on a confirmed clipboard write. This verdict also classifies failures against history.
components.usefulness: Knowing a failure repeated in the same test separates a real bug from a flaky run.
components.creativeDifference: Extends Success Check: the check is withheld until a confirmed pass, and the failure path carries comparison data.
states: initial: 'Failed · 2 of 148 tests · checkout.spec.ts', reached on load
pending: 'Attempt 2 running', reached by row 3
passed: check drawn with 'Passed on attempt n', reached on exit 0
failed-same: 'Failed again · same test', reached by the demo toggle 'Next attempt fails'
failed-different: 'Failed · different error', reached by the second demo failure
stopped: 'Stopped at n s · no verdict', reached by row 3 Stop
reduced-motion: check shown without stroke draw

components.name: Attempt history
components.description: Row of attempt chips with outcome glyph and duration that loads any past attempt's log for comparison.
components.purpose: Compare attempts of the selected step to see whether a pass was luck.
components.use: A developer selects attempt 1 after attempt 2 passes and sees the same test took 4900 ms in the pass.
components.input: Click or tap a chip. Keyboard: Tab into the row, Left and Right move, Home and End jump, Enter selects.
components.outcome: The row 2 log shows the chosen attempt read-only with a 'Viewing attempt 1 · 14:52' bar. The latest attempt is selected after each run.
components.recovery: 'Back to latest' in the bar, or Escape, returns to the newest attempt. History is kept per step and cleared only when the demo is reset.
components.mechanism: A horizontal listbox with roving tabindex. Chips have a fixed 72px width and show glyph, attempt number and duration. Over 5 attempts the row scrolls horizontally with the selected chip kept in view. Each attempt record stores its lines, failing tests and slowest test timing.
components.nearestAnalogue: 2026-10-28 pin pair compared two chart points. This row compares whole runs of one step over time.
components.usefulness: A single pass after a timeout proves little. Seeing the slowest test time across attempts shows how close it came.
components.creativeDifference: History works as a side door into the log, so comparing never leaves the panel or replaces the live view.
states: single: one chip 'Attempt 1 · failed', reached on load
latest-selected: newest chip with accent edge, reached after each run
viewing-past: older chip selected with read-only bar in row 2
overflow: horizontal scroll over 5 attempts
focus: 2px ring on chip
empty: 'No attempts for Lint yet', reached on a step with no recorded attempts

demo.sharedState: One run record for web-app #482 holds six steps, each with a status, duration and attempts array. Each attempt holds log lines, failing test names and slowest test ms. Row 1 sets the selected step. Rows 2 and 6 read that step's attempts. Row 4 sets the scope list that row 3 runs. Row 3 appends an attempt, row 2 streams it, and row 1 shows the running glyph. When the attempt ends, row 5 compares it with the previous attempt and row 6 adds a chip. A demo toggle 'Next attempt fails' switches the seeded outcome between pass (attempt 2, 39 s, slowest 4900 ms) and the same checkout.spec.ts timeout.
